correctness.rationale: Every terminal-to-terminal arm is a length L geodesic giving 2m upper bound. Chosen symmetric levels a,b=L+1-a are feasible by classifying all shortest-path routes and excluding three chosen edges via x+y constraints. At maximum every arm has two edges a_i,b_i; violating b_i+a_j>=L+1 or a_i+b_j<=L+1 creates an explicit three-edge geodesic. The cross constraints force a_i+b_j=L+1 for all distinct i,j; m>=3 synchronizes all levels and gives floor(L/2) distinct sets. Actual standard-library checker exhaustively verifies small graphs with an independent shortest-path enumerator. Finite checks are not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The available founding, geodesic-cover, small-value, and closely related theta-subgraph literature yields neither the exact classification of all maximum edge-general-position sets of equal-arm theta graphs nor the count independent of the arm number. The numeric upper bound follows from [2], but equality and rigidity require the new two-pole inequalities. Extensive actual indexed searches of statement/alias/implication variants and prior own-claim deduplication found no covering theorem. Residual unindexed-literature risk remains.

value.rationale: The exact structural classification and optimum count solve a natural two-terminal network optimization family of unbounded path lengths and arm counts. Existing path-geodesic-cover bounds do not explain when equality holds or the number and shape of all extremizers. The theorem proves global edge-level synchrony forced solely by shortest-path constraints; exactly floor(L/2) maxima independently of m. Boundary m>=3 is substantively used; this is neither a direct exercise from the cover bound nor a computation of an arbitrary finite slice.
